WP-01: Vite + React + TypeScript scaffold; Vitest; ESLint + Prettier; wrangler.jsonc
for Cloudflare Workers static assets; npm scripts (dev, build, test, lint, typecheck,
deploy); the logging abstraction (pick loglevel/tslog or our own abstraction) with the
debug-flag mechanism; fill in the README Development section. We obviously don't want to log
sensitive information.

WP-02: the frozen engine contract — ParsedSession, AnalysisResult, the worker message
protocol, and the pricing.json schema. BEFORE freezing, do the required inspection of a
real session log: use transcripts/004-build-plan/session.jsonl (it contains a real
subagent sidechain from an agent run) to verify it works  Record the findings in the contract's comments. The contract must pin
down the unknown-model degradation policy and mixed-TTL write handling per the plan
(§2), with the thresholds as named constants. Mark the insight-event taxonomy as the
one amendable section.

Acceptance: npm run build && npm test green; wrangler dev serves the placeholder app;
a stub engine returning canned data satisfies the contract end-to-end through a stub
worker; inspection findings recorded.

Work on a new branch off main, one PR, and use Conventional Commits. When CodeRabbit reviews
the PR, verify each finding for accuracy before applying it — report agree/disagree
with reasons and note anything you reject. If the log inspection contradicts an
assumption in docs/PLAN.md, update the plan in the same PR and say so explicitly.

content.content:
1	# Build plan
2	
3	The plan for taking cache-ttl-analyzer from scaffolding to a deployed MVP.
4	Grounded in the research at
5	[docs/design/claude-code-session-logs/feasibility.md](design/claude-code-session-logs/feasibility.md)
6	(referenced below as "the feasibility doc") — read it before implementing the
7	parser or simulator; it documents the traps that make naive implementations
8	silently wrong.
9	
10	This plan is decomposed into **work packages (WPs)** sized for individual Claude
11	sessions, with an explicit dependency graph so independent WPs can run in
12	parallel.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. MVP definition
17	
18	A static web app, deployed to Cloudflare, where a user:
19	
20	1. Uploads **one Claude Code session log (JSONL)** at a time — or loads a
21	   bundled sample.
22	2. Watches analysis run **entirely in their browser** (Web Worker), with a
23	   progress indicator and a cancel button.
24	3. Gets a verdict: what the session actually cost at published Anthropic API
25	   rates, what it *would have cost* under the other cache TTL (5m vs 1h), and a
26	   recommendation.
27	4. Sees cache-behavior insights: cache invalidations (expiry gaps, and hard
28	   resets from model / effort / version changes), warm-read counts, and short
29	   educational explanations of each.
30	5. Can revisit sessions analyzed earlier in the same browser session
31	   (in-memory history only — nothing persisted).
32	
33	Plus: clear instructions for finding session logs on macOS and Windows, a
34	prominent privacy statement ("analysis is local; this is open source — verify
35	it yourself" with a link to the repo), a dedicated **data policy page** (see
36	§3a), and a "prices as of" date on every dollar figure.
37	
38	Two cross-cutting requirements, cheap now and expensive to retrofit:
39	
40	- **Localization-ready from day one.** MVP ships English only, but no
41	  user-facing string is hard-coded in a component: all copy lives in locale
42	  resource files (react-i18next or equivalent — chosen in WP-07), and all
43	  number, currency, date, and duration formatting goes through the `Intl`
44	  APIs keyed to the active locale. Adding a second language later must be a
45	  translation task, not a refactor.
46	- **Data policy page**: a first-class page, linked from the footer and the
47	  upload screen, stating in plain language: analysis runs entirely in the
48	  browser; the file is never uploaded, stored, or sent anywhere; the strict
49	  CSP enforces this at the platform level (with a one-line "check devtools"
50	  pointer); no analytics or tracking in the MVP; the project is open source
51	  (repo link); and any future optional API-powered analysis will be opt-in
52	  with an explicit, itemized disclosure of what would be sent.
53	
54	### Non-goals for MVP (deferred, in rough priority order)
55	
56	- **Anthropic API deep-analysis feature** (upload timestamps/token counts for
57	  richer analysis). Deferred until MVP proves useful. When picked up, the
58	  BYO-API-key vs. our-key-plus-rate-limiting decision gets made then.
59	- Multi-file / folder upload and cross-session rollups (requires global dedup
60	  and cross-session cache modeling — feasibility doc §6.3, §7).
61	- Provider-specific rate tables (Bedrock, Vertex). MVP uses Anthropic
62	  published API rates only — see decision log.
63	- Claude Code **web JSON export** input. Unverified that it carries `usage`
64	  (feasibility doc §10). JSONL only for MVP.
65	- Durable persistence, accounts, authentication.
66	- In-app billing-mode questionnaire (feasibility §3 suggests asking the user;
67	  MVP states the API-rates framing as a label instead — see D12).
68	- Hybrid-TTL guidance (1h stable prefix + 5m tail, feasibility §10) — the
69	  logs can't support a computed number, only qualitative advice; revisit
70	  post-MVP.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## 2. Architecture
75	
76	- **Stack:** React + TypeScript + Vite. Deployed as **static assets on
77	  Cloudflare Workers** via Wrangler. **No server-side code in the MVP** — this
78	  is deliberate: the strongest form of the privacy claim is that there is no
79	  backend to send data to.
80	- **Analysis engine** (`src/engine/`): pure TypeScript, zero DOM/React
81	  dependencies, so it runs in a Web Worker and is unit-testable in Node.
82	  - **Parser** reads only the fields it needs (`type`, `timestamp`,
83	    `message.id`, `message.model`, `message.usage`, `isSidechain`, `effort`,
84	    `version`, plus `uuid`/`parentUuid` for sidechain threading and
85	    `sessionId`/`cwd`/`gitBranch` for the identification card) and **never
86	    reads `message.content`** — enforced by a test that
87	    feeds a session whose content blocks are poison values and asserts they
88	    never appear in any output (feasibility doc §9). One deliberate, named
89	    exception: the `ai-title` record (the short session title Claude Code
90	    generates), read for the session identification card (§3) — a single
91	    string, not conversation content. Not every session has one (4 of 7 in
92	    the research corpus); payload shape to be verified in WP-03.
93	  - **Simulator** implements the counterfactual model from the feasibility
94	    doc: see §3 below.
95	- **Web Worker** wraps the engine: streams the file
96	  (`File.stream()` + line splitting, so large logs don't need one giant
97	  string), posts progress messages, and supports cancellation (terminate).
98	- **Pricing config** (`src/config/pricing.json`): per-model base rates, cache
99	  multipliers (read 0.1×, 5m write 1.25×, 1h write 2.0×), `service_tier` and
100	  `speed` modifiers, and a top-level `pricesAsOf` date shown in the UI.
101	  Unknown model IDs are reported to the user, never guessed; degradation
102	  policy: unpriced requests are excluded and disclosed, their share measured
103	  in **total tokens (input + cache + output) across deduped requests**, and
104	  the verdict is suppressed when that share exceeds **10%** (both the metric
105	  and the constant are named in the WP-02 contract so verdicts are
106	  deterministic).
107	- **UI** consumes a frozen engine contract (WP-02) so UI and engine work can
108	  proceed in parallel.
109	- **Logging** goes through a small leveled abstraction (`loglevel`, `tslog`,
110	  or a thin wrapper — chosen in WP-01), used everywhere including the worker
111	  (worker log events forwarded to the main thread). Quiet by default in
112	  production; a debug flag (query param or `localStorage` toggle, documented
113	  on the data policy page) elevates verbosity so users can self-serve
114	  troubleshooting output. **Console-only, never shipped anywhere** — remote
115	  log collection would contradict the CSP/privacy stance. Anything the user
116	  needs to act on (skipped records, warnings) still surfaces in the UI, not
117	  just the log.
118	
119	### Input validation and secure file handling
120	
121	The app is static and client-side, so the threat model is a malicious or
122	corrupted **file** being processed in the user's own browser — plus proving to
123	users that nothing is exfiltrated. Rules:
124	
125	- **Three validation verdicts:** *valid*; *valid with warnings* (skipped
126	  records, out-of-range version, unknown model); or *not a session log* — no
127	  assistant rows carrying `usage`, or malformed lines exceeding **10% of
128	  non-empty lines** (an exact named constant in the WP-02 contract) — with a
129	  plain-language error, never a garbage analysis.
130	- **Numeric hygiene:** every usage field is checked finite and non-negative
131	  before pricing; bad rows are skipped and counted.
132	- **Log-derived strings are untrusted input.** Title, `cwd`, `gitBranch`,
133	  model IDs render only as text nodes (no `innerHTML` anywhere), length-clamped.
134	- **No raw JSON into app state.** The parser copies the needed fields into
135	  typed records and discards the parsed object — no spreading of parsed
136	  objects, which also neutralizes prototype-pollution keys (`__proto__`,
137	  `constructor`).
138	- **Resource limits:** file-size cap with a clear message; streaming parse
139	  with a per-line length cap so one giant line can't exhaust tab memory;
140	  analysis in a worker so the page stays responsive; cancel always available.
141	- **CSP as proof, not just promise:** deploy with a strict
142	  Content-Security-Policy (`default-src 'self'`; no external `connect-src`)
143	  so "your data never leaves the browser" is enforced by the platform and
144	  verifiable in devtools — and mention that in the privacy statement.
145	- **Nothing persisted:** the file is never written to storage; in-memory
146	  history keeps analysis results, not file bytes.
147	
148	### Engine correctness rules (from the feasibility doc — all mandatory)
149	
150	| Rule | Source |
151	|---|---|
152	| Dedup rows on `message.id` (one row per content block, each carries full usage; up to 13× overstatement otherwise) | §6.1 |
153	| Exclude `message.model == "<synthetic>"` rows | §6.2 |
154	| Partition sidechains **per subagent thread**, not as one boolean bucket: parallel subagents interleave their `isSidechain: true` rows but each has its own cache namespace. Thread identification (likely `parentUuid`/`uuid` chains) is verified against a real multi-subagent log before the WP-02 freeze | §6.4 + review |
155	| Hard cache reset on any change of `model`, `effort`, or `version`, independent of elapsed time | §6.6 |
156	| Price per request (models/tiers/speed can vary mid-session); honor `service_tier` and `speed` | §6.5 |
157	| Gap timing: use the preceding `user` row's timestamp **from the same cache thread** as request start (interleaved subagent rows make "preceding" thread-relative); fall back to the assistant row's own timestamp when the thread has none | §7 + review |
158	| Expiry model is all-or-nothing per gap; this is conservative toward 5m — disclose it in the UI | §7 |
159	| Effective TTL comes from `usage.cache_creation` (`ephemeral_5m` / `ephemeral_1h` split). Counterfactuals reprice **only the user-controllable share**; server-tool 5m writes stay at 5m in both scenarios and are tracked as their own expiry class. The reconciliation check (§5) replays each request with its **observed per-request split**, not a single session-wide TTL | §2 + review |
160	| Unrecognized record types are skipped and counted, surfaced as "N records skipped" | §4 |
161	| Warn (don't fail) when `version` is outside the validated range | §4 |
162	
163	---
164	
165	## 3. What the analysis reports
166	
167	**First, a session identification card** so the user can confirm they loaded
168	the session they intended — built entirely from content-free metadata: the
169	session title (from the `ai-title` record when present), working directory
170	(`cwd`), git branch, date and time span, duration, request count, model(s),
171	Claude Code version, and file name/size. Message content is never shown; the
172	card is why it never needs to be.
173	
174	**Headline:** the main-conversation bucket. Cost at 5m vs cost at 1h,
175	recommendation, and delta — labelled as *notional cost at published Anthropic
176	API rates* with a one-line rationale (subscription users have no per-token
177	bill; API-rate framing is what an API/Bedrock/credits user pays and what
178	everyone should understand — see decision log).
179	
180	**Conditionally:** if the session contains sidechain turns, a second section
181	for the **subagent bucket** (`subagentPromptCacheTtl`), with its own
182	recommendation. When no sidechains exist, this section does not appear, and
183	the tool does not imply it evaluated subagent traffic (feasibility doc §3).
184	
185	**Insights (the educational layer):**
186	
187	- Timeline of cache events: writes, warm reads, expiries (with the gap that
188	  caused each), hard resets (annotated with the cause: model switch, effort
189	  change, version upgrade).
190	- Counts: cache invalidations, warm-read requests, wasted-write tokens.
191	- Observed effective TTL per bucket, and whether the configuration was
192	  provably explicit (the two unambiguous patterns from feasibility doc §3) —
193	  otherwise no claim about defaults.
194	- Session shape summary: request count, span, largest gap, share of gaps in
195	  the 5m–1h band (the only band where the choice matters).
196	- A pointer to Claude Code's built-in live cache stats (`/usage`, v2.1.251+)
197	  for monitoring cache behavior going forward.
198	
199	---
200	
201	## 4. Work packages
202	
203	Sized so each WP is one focused session producing one PR into `main`. Every PR
204	passes CI (typecheck, lint, tests, build) and CodeRabbit review.
205	
206	### WP-01 — Scaffold and tooling
207	**Depends on:** nothing. **Blocks:** everything.
208	Vite + React + TS app skeleton; Vitest; ESLint + Prettier; `wrangler.jsonc`
209	for Workers static assets; npm scripts (`dev`, `build`, `test`, `lint`,
210	`typecheck`, `deploy`); the logging abstraction (pick `loglevel`/`tslog` or
211	write the ~50-line wrapper) with the debug-flag mechanism; README
212	"Development" section filled in.
213	*Acceptance:* `npm run build && npm test` green; `wrangler dev` serves the
214	placeholder app.
215	
216	### WP-02 — Engine contract (do in the same session as WP-01)
217	**Depends on:** WP-01. **Blocks:** WP-03, WP-04, WP-05, WP-07, WP-08.
218	The frozen TypeScript interfaces everything else codes against:
219	`ParsedSession` (deduped request records + skip/warning counts),
220	`AnalysisResult` (per-bucket actual/counterfactual costs, recommendation,
221	insight events), the Web Worker message protocol (start / progress / cancel /
222	result / error), and the `pricing.json` schema.
223	
224	**Before freezing, inspect real session logs** to resolve the known unknowns
225	that would otherwise force amendments: the `ai-title` payload shape, the
226	user-row → assistant-row request-start pairing, and sidechain thread
227	identification (`parentUuid`/`uuid` chains) against a real multi-subagent
228	session. The contract must also pin down two semantics the analysis depends
229	on: the **unknown-model degradation policy** (excluded-and-disclosed;
230	verdict suppressed above a threshold) and **mixed-TTL write handling** in
231	counterfactuals (server tools insert their own 5m writes regardless of the
232	user's setting — default model: hold them at 5m in both scenarios as a
233	separate expiry class and reprice only the user-controllable share; WP-02
234	finalizes and documents this so the simulator is deterministic).
235	
236	Documented inline; changes after freeze require touching this plan. The
237	insight-event taxonomy is the one section expected to be amended (WP-08 and
238	WP-D consume it and will discover needs).
239	*Acceptance:* types compile; a stub engine returning canned data satisfies
240	them end-to-end through a stub worker; the pre-freeze log inspection findings
241	are recorded in the contract's comments.
242	
243	### WP-03 — Parser
244	**Depends on:** WP-02. **Parallel with:** WP-04, WP-06, WP-09.
245	Streaming JSONL parser implementing the correctness rules table (dedup,
246	synthetic exclusion, skip-and-count, version warnings, minimal field surface,
247	content-poison test) and the validation/security rules (three verdicts,
248	numeric hygiene, typed-record copying, line-length cap).
249	Validation uses hand-rolled guards: with a dozen-field surface they are less
250	code than a schema library. (Zod v4.5 was considered and rejected for this
251	hot path — a session log is thousands of lines, not enough to need it, and
252	the dependency buys nothing here. Fine elsewhere in the app if a real need
253	appears.)
254	*Acceptance:* unit tests for every rule, plus adversarial tests: malformed
255	lines, prototype-pollution keys, hostile strings in metadata fields, negative
256	/ NaN token counts, a single multi-hundred-MB line; parses a 100MB synthetic
257	file without loading it into one string (that fixture is generated by a
258	script at test time and git-ignored, never committed).
259	
260	### WP-04 — Pricing config and cost engine
261	**Depends on:** WP-02. **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-06, WP-09.
262	`pricing.json` populated from the published pricing page (with `pricesAsOf`);
263	actual-cost computation per request (base, cache read, 5m/1h writes, output,
264	tier/speed modifiers); unknown-model reporting.
265	*Acceptance:* hand-computed unit tests (values worked out on paper, not
266	generated by code) for each modifier combination.
267	
268	### WP-05 — Counterfactual simulator
269	**Depends on:** WP-03, WP-04.
270	The core product: replay the session under each TTL; per-bucket partition;
271	gap-driven expiry; hard resets; insight-event generation (§3 above).
272	*Acceptance:* unit tests for reset/expiry/refresh edge cases, plus the golden
273	fixtures from WP-06 matching to the cent.
274	
275	### WP-06 — Fixtures and golden data
276	**Depends on:** WP-02 (shapes only). **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-04.
277	Two kinds of fixtures:
278	1. **Crafted synthetic JSONL** exercising each trap: content-block
279	   duplication, synthetic rows, sidechains (including parallel subagents
280	   with interleaved rows), mid-session model switch, effort
281	   change, version change, gaps in the 5m–1h band, mixed
282	   `ephemeral_5m`/`ephemeral_1h` writes, unknown record types, unknown model —
283	   plus adversarial fixtures: a non-session JSONL, malformed lines, hostile
284	   metadata strings, prototype-pollution keys, invalid numerics.
285	2. **Real sessions generated by Claude** enacting scenarios (a tight agent
286	   loop where 5m wins; a long gap-heavy session where 1h wins; a session that
287	   switches models mid-way) — these double as the bundled samples in
288	   `public/samples/` and as end-to-end verification that the tool's verdicts
289	   match intuition.
290	
291	**Bring `prototype-sim.py` to full parity with the §2 correctness-rules
292	table first** — as written it implements almost none of it (no sidechain
293	partition, no hard resets on model/effort/version, no `service_tier`/`speed`
294	modifiers, gap timing from the wrong timestamp, unknown models silently
295	priced as Opus, stale price table) — verified by its own hand-computed
296	tests. Only then have it emit expected-output JSON per fixture; commit those
297	as golden files with a test harness that runs the TS engine against them.
298	This makes the Python sim an independently written second implementation,
299	not a trusted oracle: disagreements are settled by hand computation (see §5).
300	*Acceptance:* golden files committed; harness wired into `npm test`; includes
301	a **captured real subagent session (with parallel subagents)** and a
302	**captured 5m-configured session** (every corpus session ran at 1h — the
303	expiry-heavy path must be exercised by real data too); real captures are
304	content-scrubbed by a script (adapt the redaction scripts from this repo's
305	`publish-transcript` skill) since they ship publicly.
306	
307	### WP-D — UX design (Claude Design session)
308	**Depends on:** nothing (MVP definition in this plan is the brief).
309	**Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-04, WP-06, WP-09.
310	A dedicated **Claude Design** session produces the visual direction and screen
311	designs for the whole flow: landing page (privacy statement, upload,
312	"find your logs" instructions, samples), the analyzing state (progress +
313	cancel), and the results view (session identification card, recommendation
314	card, cost comparison,
315	conditional subagent section, cache-event timeline, educational explainers,
316	session-history strip). It should also cover the empty/error states: unknown
317	model, skipped records, version warning, malformed file. Include the data
318	policy page, and design copy areas with text expansion in mind (translated
319	strings run ~30% longer than English). **Constraint from the strict CSP:**
320	no external assets — fonts are self-hosted or system stacks, no external
321	webfonts, CDN images, or third-party embeds; a design that depends on them
322	would force weakening the privacy-proving CSP.
323	Exports (screens, and the canvas link) are committed to `docs/design/` so
324	WP-07 and WP-08 sessions can implement against them without guessing.
325	*Acceptance:* every screen and state listed above has a design in
326	`docs/design/`; user has signed off on the direction.
327	
328	### WP-07 — UI shell
329	**Depends on:** WP-02; WP-D (visual design).
330	**Parallel with:** WP-05.
331	Upload (drag-drop + picker), Web Worker wiring with progress bar and cancel,
332	in-memory history of this browser session's analyses, "find your logs"
333	instructions (macOS: `~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl`;
334	Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\projects\...`; both moved by
335	`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set; note the 30-day default cleanup), privacy statement with repo
336	link, data policy page, sample-session loader. File-size cap and the three
337	validation verdicts (valid / warnings / not a session log) as distinct UI
338	states. Sets up the i18n foundation: locale resource files, the translation
339	hook pattern, and `Intl`-based formatters — every string in WP-07 and WP-08
340	goes through it (English-only catalog for MVP).
341	*Acceptance:* full flow works against the WP-02 stub engine; cancel actually
342	terminates the worker mid-parse; a non-session file gets the plain-language
343	rejection, not a broken analysis.
344	
345	### WP-08 — Results and insights UI
346	**Depends on:** WP-05, WP-07, WP-D.
347	Session identification card (title/`cwd`/branch/span/models, with
348	metadata-only fallback when `ai-title` is absent), recommendation card (with
349	the API-rates framing line and `pricesAsOf` date), cost comparison, conditional subagent section, cache-event timeline,
350	educational explainers, approximation disclosure (§7 conservatism), skipped
351	records / version warnings surfaced.
352	*Acceptance:* renders correctly for each WP-06 sample, including the
353	no-sidechain and unknown-model cases.
354	
355	### WP-09 — CI/CD
356	**Depends on:** WP-01. **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-04, WP-06.
357	GitHub Actions: PR workflow (typecheck, lint, test, build) required on
358	`main`; deploy workflow on push to `main` via `wrangler deploy` using a
359	Cloudflare API token secret. Document secret setup in README. Branch
360	protection on `main`. Serve the strict CSP and security headers (via the
361	Workers static-assets headers config). Once the domain is in the Cloudflare
362	account, attach
363	**cacheanalyzer.com** as a custom domain on the Worker (wrangler
364	`routes`/custom domain config).
365	*Acceptance:* a PR shows the checks; a merge to `main` deploys, reachable at
366	`workers.dev` (and at cacheanalyzer.com once DNS is live); a post-deploy
367	smoke check asserts the exact security headers on the live site
368	(`Content-Security-Policy` present with `default-src 'self'` and no external
369	`connect-src`) so a misconfigured headers file fails the deploy rather than
370	silently voiding the privacy proof; the README's Live URL is updated.
371	
372	### WP-10 — Launch polish
373	**Depends on:** WP-08, WP-09.
374	README rewrite for end users; verify samples load on the deployed site;
375	cross-browser pass (Chrome plus at least one of Safari/Firefox — the real
376	compatibility risk is `File.stream()` in workers; Edge is Chromium); perf
377	sanity check with the generated 100MB fixture; final wording pass on privacy
378	and approximation disclosures.
379	
380	### Dependency graph
381	
382	```mermaid
383	graph LR
384	    WP01[WP-01 Scaffold] --> WP02[WP-02 Contract]
385	    WP01 --> WP09[WP-09 CI/CD]
386	    WP02 --> WP03[WP-03 Parser]
387	    WP02 --> WP04[WP-04 Pricing]
388	    WP02 --> WP06[WP-06 Fixtures]
389	    WP02 --> WP07[WP-07 UI shell]
390	    WP03 --> WP05[WP-05 Simulator]
391	    WP04 --> WP05
392	    WP06 --> WP05
393	    WP05 --> WP08[WP-08 Results UI]
394	    WP07 --> WP08
395	    WP08 --> WP10[WP-10 Launch]
396	    WP09 --> WP10
397	    WPD([WP-D Claude Design]) --> WP07
398	    WPD --> WP08
399	```
400	
401	**Suggested waves:** ① WP-01+02 (one session) → ② WP-03, WP-04, WP-06, WP-09,
402	and WP-D (the Claude Design session), all in parallel → ③ WP-05 and WP-07 in
403	parallel → ④ WP-08 → ⑤ WP-10.
404	
405	---
406	
407	## 5. Testing strategy
408	
409	- **Unit tests** (Vitest) on parser rules and pricing math, with
410	  hand-computed expected values.
411	- **Golden-fixture cross-validation:** the spec-parity Python simulator
412	  (WP-06) is an independently written second implementation; the TS engine
413	  must reproduce its outputs to the cent on every fixture. Neither
414	  implementation is the oracle — hand-computed tests are the tiebreaker, so
415	  a shared logic bug can't hide in both.
416	- **Actual-vs-simulated reconciliation:** the actual cost is computed exactly
417	  from observed usage; running the simulator at the *observed* TTL must
418	  reproduce it (within the stated approximation) on every fixture — a free
419	  sanity check on the whole simulator.
420	- **Content-poison test:** proves `message.content` never influences or leaks
421	  into output.
422	- **Format-drift canary:** fixtures are tagged with the Claude Code `version`
423	  they represent; the parser's validated-version range lives in one constant,
424	  and CI fails if a golden fixture's version falls outside it. One
425	  deliberately out-of-range fixture is **exempt from the canary** and instead
426	  asserts the warn-don't-fail path, so the two rules never conflict.
427	
428	---
429	
430	## 6. Decision log
431	
432	| # | Decision | Rationale |
433	|---|---|---|
434	| D1 | Anthropic API feature deferred to post-MVP | Keeps MVP fully static: no backend, no rate limiting, strongest privacy story. (User, 2026-08-30) |
435	| D2 | All dollar figures at published Anthropic API rates, clearly labelled | API rates are what usage-billed users pay and what everyone should understand; rationale stated in README and UI. Provider tables (Bedrock/Vertex) deferred. (User) |
436	| D3 | One session upload at a time; in-memory history only | Processing time unknown; persistence deferred until the tool proves useful. (User) |
437	| D4 | Always partition sidechains in the simulation; headline the main bucket; show a subagent section only when the session contains sidechain turns | Partitioning is required for correctness regardless (§6.4); conditional display gives two-bucket value without confusing the majority whose sessions have no subagents. (Claude's vote, accepted) |
438	| D5 | Rates live in a committed `pricing.json` with a `pricesAsOf` date; unknown models reported to the user | Simple, auditable, no runtime fetch. API-driven rates possible later. (User) |
439	| D6 | Fixtures are synthetic + Claude-generated scenario sessions; no personal sessions bundled | Avoids publishing usage patterns; scenarios can be engineered to teach specific lessons and to verify verdicts. (User) |
440	| D7 | The Python simulator — brought to full spec parity in WP-06 — is an **independently written second implementation** generating golden fixtures the TS engine must match; hand-computed tests are the tiebreaker | Re-scoped after independent review: the original prototype implements almost none of the correctness rules and was never a valid oracle. Cross-validation still catches divergent bugs. (Claude's vote, revised) |
441	| D8 | Domain is **cacheanalyzer.com** (user purchasing, 2026-08-30). Deploys target `workers.dev` until the custom domain is wired up in WP-09 | Name was available; buying via Cloudflare Registrar keeps DNS in the same account as the Worker. (User) |
442	| D9 | JSONL input only for MVP | Web-export JSON unverified for `usage` data (feasibility §10). |
443	| D10 | Localization-ready architecture from day one; English-only catalog for MVP | Externalized strings + `Intl` formatting are cheap now and a painful retrofit; future languages become translation tasks. (User, 2026-08-30) |
444	| D11 | Dedicated data policy page in the MVP | Data privacy is a core product value; the policy also pre-commits the disclosure standard for any future opt-in API feature. (User, 2026-08-30) |
445	| D12 | No in-app billing-mode questionnaire; the API-rates framing is a stated label | Deliberate simplification of feasibility §3's "ask the user, don't guess"; revisit if users report confusion. (Post-review, 2026-08-30) |
446	| D13 | All logging through a leveled abstraction with a user-accessible debug flag; console-only, no remote collection | Troubleshooting a client-only app depends on users' consoles; remote logging would contradict the privacy stance. (User, 2026-08-30) |
447	
448	## 7. Risks
449	
450	| Risk | Mitigation |
451	|---|---|
452	| Log format is officially internal and unstable (feasibility §4) | Minimal field surface; version pinning + warning; skip-and-count; versioned fixtures in CI |
453	| Pricing goes stale | `pricesAsOf` shown to users; single-file update path; periodic check noted in README |
454	| Counterfactual is approximate (all-or-nothing expiry, feasibility §7) | Conservative direction (understates 1h's downside cases toward 5m) disclosed in the UI |
455	| Subagent path untested against real data | WP-06 must include a real subagent session fixture before WP-05 is called done |
456	| Huge session files stall the browser | Streaming parse in a worker; progress + cancel; 100MB perf test in WP-10 |
457	| Malicious or corrupted uploads (hostile strings, pollution keys, giant lines, non-session files) | Validation verdicts; text-node-only rendering; typed-record copying; size/line caps; adversarial fixtures in WP-03/WP-06; strict CSP |

# Build plan

The plan for taking cache-ttl-analyzer from scaffolding to a deployed MVP.
Grounded in the research at
[docs/design/claude-code-session-logs/feasibility.md](design/claude-code-session-logs/feasibility.md)
(referenced below as "the feasibility doc") — read it before implementing the
parser or simulator; it documents the traps that make naive implementations
silently wrong.

This plan is decomposed into **work packages (WPs)** sized for individual Claude
sessions, with an explicit dependency graph so independent WPs can run in
parallel.

---

## 1. MVP definition

A static web app, deployed to Cloudflare, where a user:

1. Uploads **one Claude Code session log (JSONL)** at a time — or loads a
   bundled sample.
2. Watches analysis run **entirely in their browser** (Web Worker), with a
   progress indicator and a cancel button.
3. Gets a verdict: what the session actually cost at published Anthropic API
   rates, what it *would have cost* under the other cache TTL (5m vs 1h), and a
   recommendation.
4. Sees cache-behavior insights: cache invalidations (expiry gaps, and hard
   resets from model / effort / version changes), warm-read counts, and short
   educational explanations of each.
5. Can revisit sessions analyzed earlier in the same browser session
   (in-memory history only — nothing persisted).

Plus: clear instructions for finding session logs on macOS and Windows, a
prominent privacy statement ("analysis is local; this is open source — verify
it yourself" with a link to the repo), a dedicated **data policy page** (see
§3a), and a "prices as of" date on every dollar figure.

Two cross-cutting requirements, cheap now and expensive to retrofit:

- **Localization-ready from day one.** MVP ships English only, but no
  user-facing string is hard-coded in a component: all copy lives in locale
  resource files (react-i18next or equivalent — chosen in WP-07), and all
  number, currency, date, and duration formatting goes through the `Intl`
  APIs keyed to the active locale. Adding a second language later must be a
  translation task, not a refactor.
- **Data policy page**: a first-class page, linked from the footer and the
  upload screen, stating in plain language: analysis runs entirely in the
  browser; the file is never uploaded, stored, or sent anywhere; the strict
  CSP enforces this at the platform level (with a one-line "check devtools"
  pointer); no analytics or tracking in the MVP; the project is open source
  (repo link); and any future optional API-powered analysis will be opt-in
  with an explicit, itemized disclosure of what would be sent.

### Non-goals for MVP (deferred, in rough priority order)

- **Anthropic API deep-analysis feature** (upload timestamps/token counts for
  richer analysis). Deferred until MVP proves useful. When picked up, the
  BYO-API-key vs. our-key-plus-rate-limiting decision gets made then.
- Multi-file / folder upload and cross-session rollups (requires global dedup
  and cross-session cache modeling — feasibility doc §6.3, §7).
- Provider-specific rate tables (Bedrock, Vertex). MVP uses Anthropic
  published API rates only — see decision log.
- Claude Code **web JSON export** input. Unverified that it carries `usage`
  (feasibility doc §10). JSONL only for MVP.
- Durable persistence, accounts, authentication.
- In-app billing-mode questionnaire (feasibility §3 suggests asking the user;
  MVP states the API-rates framing as a label instead — see D12).
- Hybrid-TTL guidance (1h stable prefix + 5m tail, feasibility §10) — the
  logs can't support a computed number, only qualitative advice; revisit
  post-MVP.

---

## 2. Architecture

- **Stack:** React + TypeScript + Vite. Deployed as **static assets on
  Cloudflare Workers** via Wrangler. **No server-side code in the MVP** — this
  is deliberate: the strongest form of the privacy claim is that there is no
  backend to send data to.
- **Analysis engine** (`src/engine/`): pure TypeScript, zero DOM/React
  dependencies, so it runs in a Web Worker and is unit-testable in Node.
  - **Parser** reads only the fields it needs (`type`, `timestamp`,
    `message.id`, `message.model`, `message.usage`, `isSidechain`, `effort`,
    `version`, plus `uuid`/`parentUuid` for sidechain threading and
    `sessionId`/`cwd`/`gitBranch` for the identification card) and **never
    reads `message.content`** — enforced by a test that
    feeds a session whose content blocks are poison values and asserts they
    never appear in any output (feasibility doc §9). One deliberate, named
    exception: the `ai-title` record (the short session title Claude Code
    generates), read for the session identification card (§3) — a single
    string, not conversation content. Not every session has one (4 of 7 in
    the research corpus); payload shape to be verified in WP-03.
  - **Simulator** implements the counterfactual model from the feasibility
    doc: see §3 below.
- **Web Worker** wraps the engine: streams the file
  (`File.stream()` + line splitting, so large logs don't need one giant
  string), posts progress messages, and supports cancellation (terminate).
- **Pricing config** (`src/config/pricing.json`): per-model base rates, cache
  multipliers (read 0.1×, 5m write 1.25×, 1h write 2.0×), `service_tier` and
  `speed` modifiers, and a top-level `pricesAsOf` date shown in the UI.
  Unknown model IDs are reported to the user, never guessed; degradation
  policy: unpriced requests are excluded and disclosed, their share measured
  in **total tokens (input + cache + output) across deduped requests**, and
  the verdict is suppressed when that share exceeds **10%** (both the metric
  and the constant are named in the WP-02 contract so verdicts are
  deterministic).
- **UI** consumes a frozen engine contract (WP-02) so UI and engine work can
  proceed in parallel.
- **Logging** goes through a small leveled abstraction (`loglevel`, `tslog`,
  or a thin wrapper — chosen in WP-01), used everywhere including the worker
  (worker log events forwarded to the main thread). Quiet by default in
  production; a debug flag (query param or `localStorage` toggle, documented
  on the data policy page) elevates verbosity so users can self-serve
  troubleshooting output. **Console-only, never shipped anywhere** — remote
  log collection would contradict the CSP/privacy stance. Anything the user
  needs to act on (skipped records, warnings) still surfaces in the UI, not
  just the log.

### Input validation and secure file handling

The app is static and client-side, so the threat model is a malicious or
corrupted **file** being processed in the user's own browser — plus proving to
users that nothing is exfiltrated. Rules:

- **Three validation verdicts:** *valid*; *valid with warnings* (skipped
  records, out-of-range version, unknown model); or *not a session log* — no
  assistant rows carrying `usage`, or malformed lines exceeding **10% of
  non-empty lines** (an exact named constant in the WP-02 contract) — with a
  plain-language error, never a garbage analysis.
- **Numeric hygiene:** every usage field is checked finite and non-negative
  before pricing; bad rows are skipped and counted.
- **Log-derived strings are untrusted input.** Title, `cwd`, `gitBranch`,
  model IDs render only as text nodes (no `innerHTML` anywhere), length-clamped.
- **No raw JSON into app state.** The parser copies the needed fields into
  typed records and discards the parsed object — no spreading of parsed
  objects, which also neutralizes prototype-pollution keys (`__proto__`,
  `constructor`).
- **Resource limits:** file-size cap with a clear message; streaming parse
  with a per-line length cap so one giant line can't exhaust tab memory;
  analysis in a worker so the page stays responsive; cancel always available.
- **CSP as proof, not just promise:** deploy with a strict
  Content-Security-Policy (`default-src 'self'`; no external `connect-src`)
  so "your data never leaves the browser" is enforced by the platform and
  verifiable in devtools — and mention that in the privacy statement.
- **Nothing persisted:** the file is never written to storage; in-memory
  history keeps analysis results, not file bytes.

### Engine correctness rules (from the feasibility doc — all mandatory)

| Rule | Source |
|---|---|
| Dedup rows on `message.id` (one row per content block, each carries full usage; up to 13× overstatement otherwise) | §6.1 |
| Exclude `message.model == "<synthetic>"` rows | §6.2 |
| Partition sidechains **per subagent thread**, not as one boolean bucket: parallel subagents interleave their `isSidechain: true` rows but each has its own cache namespace. Thread identification (likely `parentUuid`/`uuid` chains) is verified against a real multi-subagent log before the WP-02 freeze | §6.4 + review |
| Hard cache reset on any change of `model`, `effort`, or `version`, independent of elapsed time | §6.6 |
| Price per request (models/tiers/speed can vary mid-session); honor `service_tier` and `speed` | §6.5 |
| Gap timing: use the preceding `user` row's timestamp **from the same cache thread** as request start (interleaved subagent rows make "preceding" thread-relative); fall back to the assistant row's own timestamp when the thread has none | §7 + review |
| Expiry model is all-or-nothing per gap; this is conservative toward 5m — disclose it in the UI | §7 |
| Effective TTL comes from `usage.cache_creation` (`ephemeral_5m` / `ephemeral_1h` split). Counterfactuals reprice **only the user-controllable share**; server-tool 5m writes stay at 5m in both scenarios and are tracked as their own expiry class. The reconciliation check (§5) replays each request with its **observed per-request split**, not a single session-wide TTL | §2 + review |
| Unrecognized record types are skipped and counted, surfaced as "N records skipped" | §4 |
| Warn (don't fail) when `version` is outside the validated range | §4 |

---

## 3. What the analysis reports

**First, a session identification card** so the user can confirm they loaded
the session they intended — built entirely from content-free metadata: the
session title (from the `ai-title` record when present), working directory
(`cwd`), git branch, date and time span, duration, request count, model(s),
Claude Code version, and file name/size. Message content is never shown; the
card is why it never needs to be.

**Headline:** the main-conversation bucket. Cost at 5m vs cost at 1h,
recommendation, and delta — labelled as *notional cost at published Anthropic
API rates* with a one-line rationale (subscription users have no per-token
bill; API-rate framing is what an API/Bedrock/credits user pays and what
everyone should understand — see decision log).

**Conditionally:** if the session contains sidechain turns, a second section
for the **subagent bucket** (`subagentPromptCacheTtl`), with its own
recommendation. When no sidechains exist, this section does not appear, and
the tool does not imply it evaluated subagent traffic (feasibility doc §3).

**Insights (the educational layer):**

- Timeline of cache events: writes, warm reads, expiries (with the gap that
  caused each), hard resets (annotated with the cause: model switch, effort
  change, version upgrade).
- Counts: cache invalidations, warm-read requests, wasted-write tokens.
- Observed effective TTL per bucket, and whether the configuration was
  provably explicit (the two unambiguous patterns from feasibility doc §3) —
  otherwise no claim about defaults.
- Session shape summary: request count, span, largest gap, share of gaps in
  the 5m–1h band (the only band where the choice matters).
- A pointer to Claude Code's built-in live cache stats (`/usage`, v2.1.251+)
  for monitoring cache behavior going forward.

---

## 4. Work packages

Sized so each WP is one focused session producing one PR into `main`. Every PR
passes CI (typecheck, lint, tests, build) and CodeRabbit review.

### WP-01 — Scaffold and tooling
**Depends on:** nothing. **Blocks:** everything.
Vite + React + TS app skeleton; Vitest; ESLint + Prettier; `wrangler.jsonc`
for Workers static assets; npm scripts (`dev`, `build`, `test`, `lint`,
`typecheck`, `deploy`); the logging abstraction (pick `loglevel`/`tslog` or
write the ~50-line wrapper) with the debug-flag mechanism; README
"Development" section filled in.
*Acceptance:* `npm run build && npm test` green; `wrangler dev` serves the
placeholder app.

### WP-02 — Engine contract (do in the same session as WP-01)
**Depends on:** WP-01. **Blocks:** WP-03, WP-04, WP-05, WP-07, WP-08.
The frozen TypeScript interfaces everything else codes against:
`ParsedSession` (deduped request records + skip/warning counts),
`AnalysisResult` (per-bucket actual/counterfactual costs, recommendation,
insight events), the Web Worker message protocol (start / progress / cancel /
result / error), and the `pricing.json` schema.

**Before freezing, inspect real session logs** to resolve the known unknowns
that would otherwise force amendments: the `ai-title` payload shape, the
user-row → assistant-row request-start pairing, and sidechain thread
identification (`parentUuid`/`uuid` chains) against a real multi-subagent
session. The contract must also pin down two semantics the analysis depends
on: the **unknown-model degradation policy** (excluded-and-disclosed;
verdict suppressed above a threshold) and **mixed-TTL write handling** in
counterfactuals (server tools insert their own 5m writes regardless of the
user's setting — default model: hold them at 5m in both scenarios as a
separate expiry class and reprice only the user-controllable share; WP-02
finalizes and documents this so the simulator is deterministic).

Documented inline; changes after freeze require touching this plan. The
insight-event taxonomy is the one section expected to be amended (WP-08 and
WP-D consume it and will discover needs).
*Acceptance:* types compile; a stub engine returning canned data satisfies
them end-to-end through a stub worker; the pre-freeze log inspection findings
are recorded in the contract's comments.

### WP-03 — Parser
**Depends on:** WP-02. **Parallel with:** WP-04, WP-06, WP-09.
Streaming JSONL parser implementing the correctness rules table (dedup,
synthetic exclusion, skip-and-count, version warnings, minimal field surface,
content-poison test) and the validation/security rules (three verdicts,
numeric hygiene, typed-record copying, line-length cap).
Validation uses hand-rolled guards: with a dozen-field surface they are less
code than a schema library. (Zod v4.5 was considered and rejected for this
hot path — a session log is thousands of lines, not enough to need it, and
the dependency buys nothing here. Fine elsewhere in the app if a real need
appears.)
*Acceptance:* unit tests for every rule, plus adversarial tests: malformed
lines, prototype-pollution keys, hostile strings in metadata fields, negative
/ NaN token counts, a single multi-hundred-MB line; parses a 100MB synthetic
file without loading it into one string (that fixture is generated by a
script at test time and git-ignored, never committed).

### WP-04 — Pricing config and cost engine
**Depends on:** WP-02. **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-06, WP-09.
`pricing.json` populated from the published pricing page (with `pricesAsOf`);
actual-cost computation per request (base, cache read, 5m/1h writes, output,
tier/speed modifiers); unknown-model reporting.
*Acceptance:* hand-computed unit tests (values worked out on paper, not
generated by code) for each modifier combination.

### WP-05 — Counterfactual simulator
**Depends on:** WP-03, WP-04.
The core product: replay the session under each TTL; per-bucket partition;
gap-driven expiry; hard resets; insight-event generation (§3 above).
*Acceptance:* unit tests for reset/expiry/refresh edge cases, plus the golden
fixtures from WP-06 matching to the cent.

### WP-06 — Fixtures and golden data
**Depends on:** WP-02 (shapes only). **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-04.
Two kinds of fixtures:
1. **Crafted synthetic JSONL** exercising each trap: content-block
   duplication, synthetic rows, sidechains (including parallel subagents
   with interleaved rows), mid-session model switch, effort
   change, version change, gaps in the 5m–1h band, mixed
   `ephemeral_5m`/`ephemeral_1h` writes, unknown record types, unknown model —
   plus adversarial fixtures: a non-session JSONL, malformed lines, hostile
   metadata strings, prototype-pollution keys, invalid numerics.
2. **Real sessions generated by Claude** enacting scenarios (a tight agent
   loop where 5m wins; a long gap-heavy session where 1h wins; a session that
   switches models mid-way) — these double as the bundled samples in
   `public/samples/` and as end-to-end verification that the tool's verdicts
   match intuition.

**Bring `prototype-sim.py` to full parity with the §2 correctness-rules
table first** — as written it implements almost none of it (no sidechain
partition, no hard resets on model/effort/version, no `service_tier`/`speed`
modifiers, gap timing from the wrong timestamp, unknown models silently
priced as Opus, stale price table) — verified by its own hand-computed
tests. Only then have it emit expected-output JSON per fixture; commit those
as golden files with a test harness that runs the TS engine against them.
This makes the Python sim an independently written second implementation,
not a trusted oracle: disagreements are settled by hand computation (see §5).
*Acceptance:* golden files committed; harness wired into `npm test`; includes
a **captured real subagent session (with parallel subagents)** and a
**captured 5m-configured session** (every corpus session ran at 1h — the
expiry-heavy path must be exercised by real data too); real captures are
content-scrubbed by a script (adapt the redaction scripts from this repo's
`publish-transcript` skill) since they ship publicly.

### WP-D — UX design (Claude Design session)
**Depends on:** nothing (MVP definition in this plan is the brief).
**Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-04, WP-06, WP-09.
A dedicated **Claude Design** session produces the visual direction and screen
designs for the whole flow: landing page (privacy statement, upload,
"find your logs" instructions, samples), the analyzing state (progress +
cancel), and the results view (session identification card, recommendation
card, cost comparison,
conditional subagent section, cache-event timeline, educational explainers,
session-history strip). It should also cover the empty/error states: unknown
model, skipped records, version warning, malformed file. Include the data
policy page, and design copy areas with text expansion in mind (translated
strings run ~30% longer than English). **Constraint from the strict CSP:**
no external assets — fonts are self-hosted or system stacks, no external
webfonts, CDN images, or third-party embeds; a design that depends on them
would force weakening the privacy-proving CSP.
Exports (screens, and the canvas link) are committed to `docs/design/` so
WP-07 and WP-08 sessions can implement against them without guessing.
*Acceptance:* every screen and state listed above has a design in
`docs/design/`; user has signed off on the direction.

### WP-07 — UI shell
**Depends on:** WP-02; WP-D (visual design).
**Parallel with:** WP-05.
Upload (drag-drop + picker), Web Worker wiring with progress bar and cancel,
in-memory history of this browser session's analyses, "find your logs"
instructions (macOS: `~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl`;
Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\projects\...`; both moved by
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set; note the 30-day default cleanup), privacy statement with repo
link, data policy page, sample-session loader. File-size cap and the three
validation verdicts (valid / warnings / not a session log) as distinct UI
states. Sets up the i18n foundation: locale resource files, the translation
hook pattern, and `Intl`-based formatters — every string in WP-07 and WP-08
goes through it (English-only catalog for MVP).
*Acceptance:* full flow works against the WP-02 stub engine; cancel actually
terminates the worker mid-parse; a non-session file gets the plain-language
rejection, not a broken analysis.

### WP-08 — Results and insights UI
**Depends on:** WP-05, WP-07, WP-D.
Session identification card (title/`cwd`/branch/span/models, with
metadata-only fallback when `ai-title` is absent), recommendation card (with
the API-rates framing line and `pricesAsOf` date), cost comparison, conditional subagent section, cache-event timeline,
educational explainers, approximation disclosure (§7 conservatism), skipped
records / version warnings surfaced.
*Acceptance:* renders correctly for each WP-06 sample, including the
no-sidechain and unknown-model cases.

### WP-09 — CI/CD
**Depends on:** WP-01. **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-04, WP-06.
GitHub Actions: PR workflow (typecheck, lint, test, build) required on
`main`; deploy workflow on push to `main` via `wrangler deploy` using a
Cloudflare API token secret. Document secret setup in README. Branch
protection on `main`. Serve the strict CSP and security headers (via the
Workers static-assets headers config). Once the domain is in the Cloudflare
account, attach
**cacheanalyzer.com** as a custom domain on the Worker (wrangler
`routes`/custom domain config).
*Acceptance:* a PR shows the checks; a merge to `main` deploys, reachable at
`workers.dev` (and at cacheanalyzer.com once DNS is live); a post-deploy
smoke check asserts the exact security headers on the live site
(`Content-Security-Policy` present with `default-src 'self'` and no external
`connect-src`) so a misconfigured headers file fails the deploy rather than
silently voiding the privacy proof; the README's Live URL is updated.

### WP-10 — Launch polish
**Depends on:** WP-08, WP-09.
README rewrite for end users; verify samples load on the deployed site;
cross-browser pass (Chrome plus at least one of Safari/Firefox — the real
compatibility risk is `File.stream()` in workers; Edge is Chromium); perf
sanity check with the generated 100MB fixture; final wording pass on privacy
and approximation disclosures.

### Dependency graph

```mermaid
graph LR
    WP01[WP-01 Scaffold] --> WP02[WP-02 Contract]
    WP01 --> WP09[WP-09 CI/CD]
    WP02 --> WP03[WP-03 Parser]
    WP02 --> WP04[WP-04 Pricing]
    WP02 --> WP06[WP-06 Fixtures]
    WP02 --> WP07[WP-07 UI shell]
    WP03 --> WP05[WP-05 Simulator]
    WP04 --> WP05
    WP06 --> WP05
    WP05 --> WP08[WP-08 Results UI]
    WP07 --> WP08
    WP08 --> WP10[WP-10 Launch]
    WP09 --> WP10
    WPD([WP-D Claude Design]) --> WP07
    WPD --> WP08
```

**Suggested waves:** ① WP-01+02 (one session) → ② WP-03, WP-04, WP-06, WP-09,
and WP-D (the Claude Design session), all in parallel → ③ WP-05 and WP-07 in
parallel → ④ WP-08 → ⑤ WP-10.

---

## 5. Testing strategy

- **Unit tests** (Vitest) on parser rules and pricing math, with
  hand-computed expected values.
- **Golden-fixture cross-validation:** the spec-parity Python simulator
  (WP-06) is an independently written second implementation; the TS engine
  must reproduce its outputs to the cent on every fixture. Neither
  implementation is the oracle — hand-computed tests are the tiebreaker, so
  a shared logic bug can't hide in both.
- **Actual-vs-simulated reconciliation:** the actual cost is computed exactly
  from observed usage; running the simulator at the *observed* TTL must
  reproduce it (within the stated approximation) on every fixture — a free
  sanity check on the whole simulator.
- **Content-poison test:** proves `message.content` never influences or leaks
  into output.
- **Format-drift canary:** fixtures are tagged with the Claude Code `version`
  they represent; the parser's validated-version range lives in one constant,
  and CI fails if a golden fixture's version falls outside it. One
  deliberately out-of-range fixture is **exempt from the canary** and instead
  asserts the warn-don't-fail path, so the two rules never conflict.

---

## 6. Decision log

| # | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Anthropic API feature deferred to post-MVP | Keeps MVP fully static: no backend, no rate limiting, strongest privacy story. (User, 2026-08-30) |
| D2 | All dollar figures at published Anthropic API rates, clearly labelled | API rates are what usage-billed users pay and what everyone should understand; rationale stated in README and UI. Provider tables (Bedrock/Vertex) deferred. (User) |
| D3 | One session upload at a time; in-memory history only | Processing time unknown; persistence deferred until the tool proves useful. (User) |
| D4 | Always partition sidechains in the simulation; headline the main bucket; show a subagent section only when the session contains sidechain turns | Partitioning is required for correctness regardless (§6.4); conditional display gives two-bucket value without confusing the majority whose sessions have no subagents. (Claude's vote, accepted) |
| D5 | Rates live in a committed `pricing.json` with a `pricesAsOf` date; unknown models reported to the user | Simple, auditable, no runtime fetch. API-driven rates possible later. (User) |
| D6 | Fixtures are synthetic + Claude-generated scenario sessions; no personal sessions bundled | Avoids publishing usage patterns; scenarios can be engineered to teach specific lessons and to verify verdicts. (User) |
| D7 | The Python simulator — brought to full spec parity in WP-06 — is an **independently written second implementation** generating golden fixtures the TS engine must match; hand-computed tests are the tiebreaker | Re-scoped after independent review: the original prototype implements almost none of the correctness rules and was never a valid oracle. Cross-validation still catches divergent bugs. (Claude's vote, revised) |
| D8 | Domain is **cacheanalyzer.com** (user purchasing, 2026-08-30). Deploys target `workers.dev` until the custom domain is wired up in WP-09 | Name was available; buying via Cloudflare Registrar keeps DNS in the same account as the Worker. (User) |
| D9 | JSONL input only for MVP | Web-export JSON unverified for `usage` data (feasibility §10). |
| D10 | Localization-ready architecture from day one; English-only catalog for MVP | Externalized strings + `Intl` formatting are cheap now and a painful retrofit; future languages become translation tasks. (User, 2026-08-30) |
| D11 | Dedicated data policy page in the MVP | Data privacy is a core product value; the policy also pre-commits the disclosure standard for any future opt-in API feature. (User, 2026-08-30) |
| D12 | No in-app billing-mode questionnaire; the API-rates framing is a stated label | Deliberate simplification of feasibility §3's "ask the user, don't guess"; revisit if users report confusion. (Post-review, 2026-08-30) |
| D13 | All logging through a leveled abstraction with a user-accessible debug flag; console-only, no remote collection | Troubleshooting a client-only app depends on users' consoles; remote logging would contradict the privacy stance. (User, 2026-08-30) |

## 7. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Log format is officially internal and unstable (feasibility §4) | Minimal field surface; version pinning + warning; skip-and-count; versioned fixtures in CI |
| Pricing goes stale | `pricesAsOf` shown to users; single-file update path; periodic check noted in README |
| Counterfactual is approximate (all-or-nothing expiry, feasibility §7) | Conservative direction (understates 1h's downside cases toward 5m) disclosed in the UI |
| Subagent path untested against real data | WP-06 must include a real subagent session fixture before WP-05 is called done |
| Huge session files stall the browser | Streaming parse in a worker; progress + cancel; 100MB perf test in WP-10 |
| Malicious or corrupted uploads (hostile strings, pollution keys, giant lines, non-session files) | Validation verdicts; text-node-only rendering; typed-record copying; size/line caps; adversarial fixtures in WP-03/WP-06; strict CSP |
